texts.preamble: The Choice Trading Corporation Ltd vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 18 March, 2014 Author: P.N.Ravindran Bench: P.N.Ravindran In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr.Justice P.N.Ravindran Tuesday,The 18Th Day Of March 2014/27Th Phalguna, 1935 WP(C).No. 7542 of 2014 (P) --------------------------- Petitioner(S): -------------------------- The Choice Trading Corporation Ltd. Represented By Its Director, Balachandran P Choice House, P.V.Sreedharan Road, Kumbalam Kochi-682 508. By Adv. Sri.Sherry J. Thomas Respondent(S): ---------------------------- 1. The Commissioner Of Customs Imports, Customs House, Kochi-9. 2. Authorized Officer Kochi Seaport And Airport Food Safety And Standards Authority Of India Ministry Of Health And Familywelfarte Of India 1St Floor Marine Building, North End Willington Island, Kochi-682 001. 3.
texts.facts: The petitioner a private limited company, engaged in the business of exporting processed sea foods, imported a consignment of Sodium Tri Poly Phosphate as per bill of entry No.3807012 dated 14.11.2013 from Belgium. Since the goods were not found to conform to the standard laid down under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Commissioner of Customs issued Ext.P6 show cause notice dated 18.12.2013 calling upon the petitioner to show cause why the goods should not be confiscated. The petitioner thereupon submitted Ext.P7 letter dated 26.12.2013 requesting the Commissioner to sent a sample to the Referral Laboratory. A sample was accordingly sent to the Referral Laboratory which issued Ext.P11 analysis report dated 6.1.2014 to the effect that the sample does not conform to the standards laid down in the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011. Thereupon, the petitioner submitted Ext.P12 representation dated 12.2.2014 before the Commissioner of Customs requesting him to waive the demurrage/detention charges accrued on the consignment, the penalty if any charged and also for permission to re-export the shipment at the earliest. The instant writ petition was thereupon filed on 14.3.2014, seeking the following reliefs:- "i) Call for the entire records pertaining to the Exhibit P3 and Exhibit P11 reports, which form the ground for rejection of NOC by the 1st Respondent. ii) Issue a writ of mandamus, any other writ, order or direction to the 1st Respondent to consider the Exhibit P 12 and allow re-export of the consignment.
texts.arguments: 2. When the writ petition came up for hearing today, Sri.Sherry J. Thomas, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Additional Commissioner of Customs, Kochi has by order passed on 10.3.2014 permitted the petitioner to re-export the goods on payment of a fine of Rs.25,000/- under section 125 of the Customs Act, 1962 and also levied a fine of Rs.5,000/- under section 112(a) of the Customs Act, 1962 and therefore, the writ petition may be disposed of reserving liberty with the petitioner to challenge Ext.P11 report of analysis in other appropriate proceedings. Sri .John Varghese, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the Central Board of Excise and Customs did not oppose the said submission.

Sri .John Varghese, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the Central Board of Excise and Customs did not oppose the said submission.
